title: State from Coordinates Finder: Name the State
description: Look up state or region fields using reverse geocoding; confirm jurisdictions with official data.
summary_sentence: The returned address field is not an authoritative point-in-boundary result, including for water and border locations.
quick_answer: This tool reverse-geocodes the chosen point using Nominatim and displays available address fields from a nearby suitable mapped object. Fields may be missing or use broader fallbacks; the result is not a verified legal boundary or a guarantee of the nearest place.
steps_intro: Coordinates are stateless. Give them their jurisdiction:

body.t: A road trip's photos sort by the state they were actually taken in — borders crossed at night included. The
refines the story; this page settles the jurisdiction.
A dataset claims Texas; a third of its points sit in Oklahoma. The finder is the audit that takes one paste per suspect point.
Sales territories, licensing regions and service areas follow state lines — a point's state is the first key every one of those joins needs.
Points near Four Corners, or along a river border, get their true containing state — geometry over the souvenir's version.
The White House's coordinates return the District of Columbia — not Maryland, not Virginia. The finder reports the jurisdiction the boundary data holds, including the ones that are not states at all.

The Mississippi's channel has wandered since its borders were drawn, leaving pockets of states on the 'wrong' bank. The polygon, not the river's current mood, decides — and the finder follows the polygon.

popular_table.note: Answers ride on boundary datasets of the Census/OpenStreetMap family. Legal jurisdiction for a disputed point belongs to surveys and courts; this is the map data's verdict, fast and named.

faq: Yes — the finder covers provinces for Canadian points in the same spirit, from the same class of boundary record.
Puerto Rico, Guam and the others are named as themselves where the boundary data carries them.
A point in the Great Lakes?
Nominatim results for water points vary with mapped data. This tool does not test authoritative water boundaries; use official sources for jurisdiction.
How close to a border can I trust it?
The tool does not perform a verified point-in-polygon boundary test. Near boundaries or for legal use, consult the responsible authority and consider coordinate uncertainty.
The county layer has its own tools — What County Am I In and the County Boundary Viewer go one level deeper.
State parks that cross state lines?
A few recreation areas straddle borders; the point's own side decides its state — the park's name is not a jurisdiction.
